tier_reason: Tier A stands on the QOIR benchmark (public code, gcc 10.2.1, flags, Debian Bullseye packages, stated CPU). Enricher corrections: the README's 'less than 6% of the time, 66% of the size' claim is against stb_image_write's stbi_write_png timed with the disk write, not libpng; the QOIR row is not smaller than libpng on every subset (icon_512 CmpRatio 0.0534 versus 0.0499); the measured binary links Debian's system libzstd rather than the vendored zstd 1.3.4; and the WangXuan95 shootout ran a modified build (PNM I/O, level switch, g++ -static -O3).

corrections.claimed_speedup: QOIR benchmark: ZPNG_Lossless encode 126.21 MPixels/s and decode 256.32 vs libpng 5.49 and 56.18 (about 23x and 4.6x, derived from page data) with smaller output overall (CmpRatio 0.2182 vs 0.2423, about 10% smaller, derived; larger on icon_512: 0.0534 vs 0.0499). README: less than 6% of the compressor's time and 66% of the size on one 13.9 MB photo, measured against stb_image_write's stbi_write_png with the disk write included, not libpng. WangXuan95 CLIC2021 shootout (modified build: PNM I/O, level switch, g++ -static -O3): ZPNG 25.909 s compress and 24.083 s decompress, 1,755,786,378 bytes vs Pillow PNG (optimize=False) 334.791 s, 33.677 s, 2,003,016,524 bytes.
corrections.caveats: Zpng is its own format (custom header plus zstd), not PNG-compatible. Smaller than libpng overall in the QOIR run (0.2182 vs 0.2423) and on most subsets (photo_kodak 0.4776 vs 0.5630, screenshot_web 0.0584 vs 0.0757) but not on icon_512 (0.0534 vs 0.0499); WebP lossless is smaller still (0.1651). The libpng baseline is Debian Bullseye's package through the simplified API with image.flags = 0 (default compression level and filter heuristic). The QOIR binary links Debian's system libzstd, not the vendored zstd 1.3.4. Decoder safety from code reading (not run): a 32-bit byteCount overflow lets a crafted 32768x32768 RGBA header plus an empty zstd frame cause heap out-of-bounds reads and writes, and the ZSTD_decompress output size is ignored so truncated files decode silently; width and height are truncated to uint16, the input StrideBytes is ignored, and 16-bit StrideBytes is wrong.
